content: If you experience any side effects, it is important to contact your doctor for medical advice. Before starting rifapentine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, other rifamycins (such as rifampin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication, as it may increase the risk of liver disease. Rifapentine can reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, rifapentine should only be used if absolutely necessary. If taken during the last few weeks of pregnancy, it may increase the risk of bleeding in both the mother and the newborn. Notify your doctor immediately if you observe any bleeding in your newborn. It is not known if rifapentine passes into breast milk, but similar drugs are known to do so. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Rifapentine may accelerate the removal of other medications from your body, potentially reducing their effectiveness. This medication may also decrease the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, which could result in pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor whether you should use additional reliable birth control methods while taking this medication. Rifapentine may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as folate and vitamin B12 levels, potentially causing inaccurate results. If someone overdoses and exhibits severe symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as sputum tests, liver function tests, bilirubin levels, and complete blood counts, should be performed to monitor your progress and detect any side effects. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you remember the next day or later, consult your doctor or pharmacist for a new dosing schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
